title: Repertoire, modal playing and a young pianist

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: You know I find with the college, the young students I'm working with, they go out, take their gigs and play their things. I find that they get so involved in learning the latest hit jazz tunes that they don't have any repertoire. I've even tried to take them, like at Christmas holiday time I took them to (unintelligible) 's school and the teachers. And, you know, they're learning songs.

Well, even the big jazz players now. You know what happens is they're playing these what they call modal tunes, they've only got two goddamned chords for 20 minutes. And that's what they're copying, songs with two chords. And that's why they don't know how to get -- and they complain, they say at Berkeley all they teach us is 2-5-1. I say, well, you need a lot more 2-5-1 because all you play is 1. You've got to get there, but they don't because all music is 2-5-1. Even Beethoven is 2-5-1.

Sure, I tell them, you're limiting yourself. You've got to learn these songs, and especially if you're a New York musician, if you expect to make a living in New York, you've got to know your instrument. If you can't get in a studio, you're going to have to take a club date. And you should also have you a Broadway show book and learn the tunes of a Broadway show.
You know, you asked me that question and you've got the answer right in your own group you're playing with.
Bob was telling us about your piano player, what's his name?

He's saying, how does this kid know all these tunes? A kid your age, you know all these old people's tunes. He says, 'My teacher made me go clear through the fake book.' Now, here's a kid, I don't know, what is 23, 26, and he's working big time. Why? He knows all the tunes.
You ask what a young musician should do. There's the answer right up there. There's a kid who hit the big time 20 years before you think he would.
Sure, he can't miss because he plays jazz with us, when he goes back to New York, if he wants to play club dates in the park or in a country club, fine.

Yeah, if he wants to play modal, that will be simple for him because he can play all the stuff with the chord changes. And there is the answer to the whole thing. You ask me about the Fake Books, come to think of it, that's exactly what they should do. Go through every damned tune in the book.
